sections.title: This Evening and Tonight:
sections.text: Fog forming readily given light winds and developing clear spells, perhaps becoming locally dense, with local frost also possible. Locally heavy showers near southern coastal districts should clear offshore during the evening to leave a drier remainder of the night.

sections.title: Sunday:
sections.text: Widely a chilly and murky start, with mist and fog only slowly lifting and clearing towards lunchtime. Some eventual sunny spells then developing. Winds staying light, with near-normal temperatures.

sections.title: Outlook for Monday to Wednesday:
sections.text: Probably dry but rather cloudy Monday after a murky start with some fog. Breezier Tuesday, with periods of rain making progress northeast, with further rain likely Wednesday. Temperatures edging upwards.

days6To15.title: UK Outlook for Thursday 12 Nov 2026 to Saturday 21 Nov 2026
days6To15.text: At the start of this period, outbreaks of rain across the south of the UK will clear away as clearer conditions spread from the north. A few wintry showers are likely in the far north, but otherwise this will mean a spell of fine and dry weather developing for most areas at the end of next week and the weekend. Over the following week, a change to more changeable weather is likely, with Atlantic frontal systems bringing rain and some strong winds. After a cold start, temperatures will probably be above average overall.

sections.text: Scattered coastal showers will come and go, but remaining dry inland. Clear spells in the south under which frost and fog will develop. Cold and cloudy further northeast.

sections.title: Sunday:
sections.text: Any fog will lift through the morning to bring long spells of sunshine. Cloudier spells further north, but for all it will feel cool, calm and autumnal.

sections.title: Outlook for Monday to Wednesday:
sections.text: A foggy, frosty and bright morning on Monday, before cloud thickens. Cloudy and breezy with spells of rain during Tuesday and Wednesday, but temperatures will be milder than previous days.

sections.text: Patchy rain will affect northern England and southern Scotland overnight. Elsewhere any showers will tend to become focussed towards coasts, allowing some clear spells to develop. Patches of fog and frost forming, the fog dense across parts of southern England.

sections.title: Sunday:
sections.text: Fog and any frost will gradually clear on Remembrance Sunday, and patchy rain will generally become confined towards northern England and eastern Scotland. Otherwise some sunshine developing, in gentle winds.

sections.title: Outlook for Monday to Wednesday:
sections.text: Mostly dry on Monday with fog and frost clearing to leave sunny spells. Wet and in places rather windy weather arriving from the southwest thereafter, reaching all but northern Scotland.

days6To15.title: UK Outlook for Thursday 12 Nov 2026 to Saturday 21 Nov 2026
days6To15.text: At the start of this period, outbreaks of rain across the south of the UK will clear away as clearer conditions spread from the north. A few wintry showers are likely in the far north, but otherwise this will mean a spell of fine and dry weather developing for most areas at the end of next week and the weekend. Over the following week, a change to more changeable weather is likely, with Atlantic frontal systems bringing rain and some strong winds. After a cold start, temperatures will probably be above average overall.

days16To30.title: UK Outlook for Sunday 22 Nov 2026 to Sunday 6 Dec 2026
days16To30.text: Changeable or unsettled conditions are expected through the last part of November. Atlantic frontal system are likely to spread across the UK, bringing some heavy rain at times and a chance of strong winds. Drier, brighter interludes are likely between systems, and it is possible conditions could become drier overall into early December. Temperatures are likely to be above normal overall.

regional.title: London & Southeast England
regional.headline: Areas of fog into Sunday morning. Some brighter weather later.

sections.title: This Evening and Tonight:
sections.text: Fog forming readily given light winds and developing clear spells, perhaps becoming locally dense, with local frost also possible. Locally heavy showers near southern coastal districts should clear offshore during the evening to leave a drier remainder of the night.

sections.title: Sunday:
sections.text: Widely a chilly and murky start, with mist and fog only slowly lifting and clearing towards lunchtime. Some eventual sunny spells then developing. Winds staying light, with near-normal temperatures.

sections.title: Outlook for Monday to Wednesday:
sections.text: Probably dry but rather cloudy Monday after a murky start with some fog. Breezier Tuesday, with periods of rain making progress northeast, with further rain likely Wednesday. Temperatures edging upwards.

regional.title: West Midlands
regional.headline: Becoming foggy into Remembrance Sunday.

sections.title: This Evening and Tonight:
sections.text: Dry with clear spells in the south, but cloudier further north, perhaps with a spot of rain. Under calm, clear skies, areas of dense fog will develop. A chilly night, or cold in rural, clear spots.

sections.title: Sunday:
sections.text: Fog will lift through the morning to bring long spells of sunshine, in the south. Cloudier further north, though it will become gradually clearer. Feeling cool, calm and dry.

sections.title: Outlook for Monday to Wednesday:
sections.text: Fog and frost on Monday morning, then sunny break. A cold start again on Tuesday, and a band of rain transits through. Midler and breezier on Wednesday, with more rain.
